provenance.citation: Kowalski, R. A. (1974). Predicate logic as programming language. IFIP Congress 74, Stockholm, pp. 569–574.
provenance.locus: Section 9 ("Database and Information Retrieval"), Figure 2 — parent/ancestor Horn-clause program and resolution trace.
provenance.notes: Kowalski 1974 Fig. 2 defines parent/ancestor relationships used to illustrate predicate logic as a programming language. This fixture exercises the Prolog8 catalog path (no ?N variable rules) using a direct parent-fact query. Facts encode parent relations; the goal queries whether bob is the parent of ann. The Prolog8 kernel loads the facts, emits a kernel-query event (required by the OCEL process conformance model), and returns Allow with selected='bob-ann'.

input.intent: prove parent(bob, ann) from the family fact base (Kowalski 1974)

expected.note: Direct fact lookup: parent(bob-ann) is in the fact base. Prolog8 kernel admits the query and returns Allow. selected = 'bob-ann' which contains 'ann', satisfying the binding check.
